action.reason: Day 1 protocol: establish baseline for pendulum_lab before any other work. This is foundational; all subsequent precision measurement depends on it. Starting with the laboratory pendulum (not observatory) keeps me in-house for initial checks and allows immediate cross-reference with the civic timekeeping ledger readings.

pendulum_lab has 14 baseline trials already—sufficient for a preliminary mean (1.6682 beats) but I need to establish drift behaviour. Running 10 post-baseline trials today will let me detect whether the instrument is stable or drifting. This is essential before I can trust any of my other comparisons. The observatory instruments (pendulum_obs, resonator_obs) have only 2 trials each and are essentially useless without more data, but pendulum_lab is my most densely measured instrument and the logical place to build confidence in the measurement programme. Once I have post-baseline data on pendulum_lab, I can assess whether calibration is holding or whether systematic drift is occurring—information I'll need for all subsequent work.

state.question: Why do measurements from different instruments and observation modes show systematic temporal offsets and sign reversals in their cross-correlations, rather than converging toward a common physical quantity?

hypotheses.label: Instrumental drift or calibration divergence between lab and observational setups
hypotheses.rationale: The cross-checks reveal consistent sign reversals and offset patterns: pendulum_lab anticorrelates with pendulum_obs (−0.596 at 4-day lag), yet pendulum_lab correlates with resonator_lab (+0.597 at 4-day lag). This suggests not random noise but systematic differences in how each instrument responds to the same physical process. The lab instruments may be drifting relative to the observational ones, or calibration baselines were not truly independent. The strongest within-instrument signal is resonator_lab echoing itself from 4 days prior (0.602), suggesting a coherent but offset temporal structure in one channel that breaks down in others.

hypotheses.label: Environmental driver with a 4–6 day period affecting lab and observational modes asymmetrically
hypotheses.rationale: Multiple offset correlations peak at 4–6 day lags (pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_lab at 4 days; pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs at 6 days; resonator_lab echoing itself at 4 days). This is not noise; it is structure.
